text:
anya: Quick sync - we need a deterministic plan for canary admission that avoids global queues and keeps fallback warm. Last spike killed tail latencies.

miguel: We should avoid head-of-line blocking by routing decisions at the edge. Proposal: probabilistic spillover + capacity tokens per model shard.

sam: Explain probabilistic spillover?

miguel: Small % of traffic (e.g., 2%) is always routed to fallback to keep it hot and exercised. Rest uses token admission. Keeps fallback caches warm without overloading.

kevin: Love that. How do tokens work? Central token store or local?

anya: Tradeoffs: central store (Redis) gives global fairness but single point; local tokens are simple and degrade gracefully. Maybe hybrid: central authoritative counts + local lease for short bursts.

liam: Lease window idea: routers fetch a token-leases batch from Redis for each shard. They consume locally and renew when low. Less chattiness and still globally bounded.

sam: Need eviction strategy for leases when a router dies. Use short TTLs and optimistic retries. Redis stream or CDC for reclaiming? TTL should be < router heartbeat interval.

anya: Also need per-tenant priority tiers. Premium tenants get higher token allotment and lower spillover prob. Defaults map to trial/standard/enterprise.

kevin: What about fallback compatibility? If fallback variant returns slightly different structured output we need a translator layer not just passthrough.

miguel: Agreed. Add a TranslationAdapter interface on the router: translate(fallback_output, model_version_target) -> normalized_response. Should be pluggable by product teams.

sam: Metrics to emit: decision_reason, route_target, token_lease_remaining, fallback_warmness_score (cache_hit_rate + recent_latency).

liam: For health signals from runtime, include: shard_available_slots, tail_p95_ms, synthetic_probe_ok. Router uses these to adjust local spillover % and token refill rates.

anya: Example adaptive rule: if p95 < 150ms and synthetic_probe_ok -> refill_rate = base_rate * 2; if p95 between 150-400ms -> refill_rate = base_rate; if p95 > 400ms -> stop refilling and increase spillover to 10%.

kevin: We should avoid oscillation. Add hysteresis windows and exponential backoff for refill changes. Also an inertia period before reversing policy.

sam: Pseudocode for router admission (high-level):

```
if tenant.overrides.allow_direct_canary: route(canary, reason=override)
else if rand() < tenant.spillover_prob: route(fallback, reason=spillover)
else if local_lease.consume(): route(canary, reason=token)
else if queue.push_with_max_wait(max_wait_ms): route(queue, reason=queued)
else: route(fallback, reason=overflow)
```

anya: Queue is low-priority best-effort. We should have per-tenant max_wait and a global soft cap on queued requests to protect other tenants.

miguel: Testing plan: 1) Synthetic burst test with canary-heavy traffic 2) Chaos test: kill router process holding leases 3) Long-tail validation: run 24h with spillover enabled and measure output quality drift.

kevin: For drift safety, run daily evals of fallback vs canary and raise an alert if output divergence exceeds threshold. Tag tenants that see higher divergence.

liam: Cost accounting: metric tokens_consumed_by_canary and fallback_invocations. Billing team needs per-tenant breakdown because fallback may use smaller cheaper models but still counts.

sam: On storage: keep lease metadata and token counters in Redis hashes, but keep recent decisions in local stats for quick debug. If Redis outage, routers fallback to conservative mode: reduce refill rates and increase spillover to 5%.

anya: Operational playbook snippets: if canary_p95 > 500ms -> set spillover to 50% and notify infra @oncall. If Redis latency > 200ms -> switch to local-lease-mode and post warning.

canary-bot: canary-bot: probe ok=1 p95_ms=98 shard_slots=12 cache_hit=0.17 at 1715130200

kevin: Nice. Also add a feature-flag to flip probabilistic spillover per-route. Default off for sensitive routes.

miguel: Security note: translator adapters must run in sandbox (wasm) to avoid untrusted code in router.

anya: Action items: miguel -> design lease format + reclaim strategy; sam -> implement local lease consumer + spillover toggle; kevin -> translation adapter spec + wasm sandbox proposal; liam -> telemetry schema and ops runbooks.

sam: I'll open a PR with a spike implementation and a harness for synthetic bursts.

kevin: I'll draft the adapter interface and an example translator for the restricted-output-case.

anya: Cool. Let's review at infra sync tomorrow and aim to enable spillover on one non-critical route in staging next week. :rocket:
